title: Completed scalar comparison preserves the inverse-image counit
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with inverse $\bar g:Y\to X$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and completed coefficient sheaves $R_{F,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ for $F=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $\mathcal C_F(W)=D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$, the derived-complete integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}:\mathcal C_F(Y)\to\mathcal C_F(X)$ and $H_F=\bar g^{-1}:\mathcal C_F(X)\to\mathcal C_F(Y)$, transporting the module actions through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Let $u_{F,K}:H_FG_FK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ be the canonical inverse-image identification: on site objects it is the reindexing identification induced by $g\bar g=\mathrm{id}_Y$.

Let $T_W:\mathcal C_E(W)\to\mathcal C_L(W)$ be integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], set $C_WK=K\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and let $\chi_W:C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W$ be the specified natural completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use the specified ordinary tensor reindexing isomorphisms $b^g:C_XG_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_Y$ and $b^{\bar g}:C_YH_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_LC_X$ of [lem-weil-isomorphism-comparison-scalar-extension], and define
$$\beta^g_K=G_L(\chi_{Y,K})b^g_K\chi_{X,G_EK}^{-1},\qquad \beta^{\bar g}_M=H_L(\chi_{X,M})b^{\bar g}_M\chi_{Y,H_EM}^{-1}.$$
For every $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$ the following are equalities of derived morphisms:
$$u_{L,C_YK}H_L(b^g_K)b^{\bar g}_{G_EK}=C_Y(u_{E,K}),$$
$$u_{L,T_YK}H_L(\beta^g_K)\beta^{\bar g}_{G_EK}=T_Y(u_{E,K}).$$
They have sources $C_YH_EG_EK$ and $T_YH_EG_EK$, respectively, and targets $C_YK$ and $T_YK$. They are natural in $K$ and use the specified $b$ and $\chi$, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between the same functors.

proof.text: Normalize the double finite constant coefficient transport against the identity-on-underlying-schemes site isomorphism. Conjugate by the inverse of the canonical reindexing isomorphism; the resulting endomorphism of the constant sheaf fixes each constant section by isoSectionwiseConstantMap_existsUnique and naturality of toSheafify. Full faithfulness of forgetting commutativity and sheafification uniqueness make it the identity. The completed coefficient maps are limit lifts. Postcompose their double transport with each finite projection, use the lift equations and the finite equality, then use naturality of the reindexing transformation and joint monicity of limit projections.

proof.text: Invert the completed coefficient equality. Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp, pushforwardCongr₂ and pushforwardId give a natural isomorphism from the double module inverse image to the identity. Its component is exactly restriction along the inverse of the specified site counit. Extensionality on each module, site object and section proves uniqueness. This constructs integralInverseImageCounit_existsUnique without a new existence assumption.

proof.text: Use the ordinary scalar model already supplied by integralOrdinaryScalarWitness; its exactness is already an instance, so no second finite-free-coordinate argument is needed. The normalized ordinary scalar adjunction identifies its unit with 1 tensor x. The injective adjunction Hom equivalence shows that maps out of this scalar extension are equal when they agree on every such unit section. Its unit naturality supplies the formulas for restriction and module maps. The specified isomorphismScalarTensor_existsUnique applied twice sends these generators to the same reindexed tensor. The section normalization of the constructed counit followed by the two unit naturality formulas proves scalarModuleCounit on all module sheaves. No equality between tensor-sheaf sections and sectionwise tensors is used.

proof.text: Prove the exact-functor descent calculation with private generic helpers. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations, and the identity factorization, identify the derived counit and derived tensor squares on Qh of each complex. The sheaf identity of the preceding step holds degreewise, hence on homotopy classes. Naturality moves all factorization isomorphisms to common source and target positions; cancel them, apply the degreewise equality, and use Localization.natTrans_ext to descend it to every derived object. Specialize to the named inverse image, scalar functors and normalized isomorphisms to obtain the ordinary clause.

proof.text: Expand the specified beta maps and precompose with chi_Y on H_E G_E K. The adjacent chi_X and its inverse cancel after H_L. Naturality of the normalized derived counit at chi_Y moves chi_Y to the output. Substitute the ordinary clause and then naturality of chi_Y at u_E. Constructibility of both successive inverse-image inputs supplies the required completeness and invertibility of chi. The existing comparison-model normalization is retained, so these are the specified completion maps.
